casual.custom: My free-scene design: a quiet solo late breakfast at a sunlit railway-station noodle counter, daytime indoors with bright even light. After tiring practice, she has discovered that her enormous steamed bun is too hot to bite, a faint wistful smile with raised inner brows. Seated sideways on a high stool, torso gently facing the viewer, she holds the bun on a small paper napkin in her right hand at chest height, right upper arm dropping from its own shoulder and elbow bent forward; her left arm drops naturally with her left palm flat on the counter. Three-quarter seated portrait from head to knees, eye-level camera, face clearly visible. Her original outfit, not in our catalog, is a saffron-yellow towel-knit strapless culotte romper: a fitted fully opaque chest band and a curved waist bridge join to broad cropped trouser legs, an oval midriff aperture and bare shoulders, secure coverage of chest and pelvis. Her pale-purple training bag with two white bands rests on the adjacent empty counter ledge; no other people, no readable signs. This is a pause over breakfast, not a workshop or equipment task.

prompt:
CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — Tyrogue (배루키) personified, fighting type. Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut and skin tone; her figure follows BODY TYPE; expression and hair motion may change.

FACE: exactly the face of the attached image — the same face shape, jawline, eye shape and size, nose, lips and their proportions, and the same skin rendering. Do not add skin texture, pores, harder nose or lip modelling, a face lengthened by the camera angle, a heavy jaw, or any facial definition the attached image does not have.

The attached image's armor hides her figure, so take her body shape from this line, not from the armor's outline; her head stays in natural adult proportion to her body.

Fine subtle linework, smooth skin shading and softly blended gradients. Layered flowing hair with carefully drawn strands and delicate highlights. Highly detailed clothing and accessories with convincing fabric weave, stitching, folds, seams, buckles and material-specific reflections. Her skin has a glossy sheen — smooth, bright specular highlights on her shoulders, collarbones, chest, arms and thighs, a polished lustrous finish over her skin tone, never wet or oily. skin_exposure: bold — more scene-appropriate shoulder, back, midriff or leg exposure; cover chest and pelvis

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face and hair — not its armor, garment, layers, sash, tassels, jewelry, hair ornaments or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; that outfit must read at first glance, keeping its own recognisable colours and parts. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her source belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her own costume, genre or palette.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same.

ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no creature beside her, no text, no lettering, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions — about 7.5 heads tall, her head in proportion to her shoulders and body. No extra limbs; her worn features are costume, never extra limbs.

MIDRIFF: wherever her stomach is bare, it shows a soft, subtle six-pack — lightly defined abdominal segments in two neat columns of three on a flat, firm, toned midriff; feminine and gently shaded, an athletic woman's abs, never a hard, deeply carved bodybuilder six-pack. If her outfit covers her stomach, keep it covered.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may leave the frame past the forearm, never floating without its arm; fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.
